intro: Trollskogen is a nature reserve at the northeastern tip of Öland, 266 hectares of pine and oak with its own visitor centre, and the oldest oak on the island grows in it. Trolleken is somewhere between 800 and 900 years old by the county administration's reckoning, reached on the 4.5-kilometre Trollskogsstigen trail from the naturum. Nobody has published a girth or a height for it. The reserve is free and open at any hour, and there is no bus: route 136 and the car park at the trailhead are how people arrive.

question_answer: Trolleken, the troll oak, standing in Trollskogen nature reserve at the northeastern tip of Öland. The county administration of Kalmar puts it at 800 to 900 years old, which makes it the oldest oak on the island. It is reached on the marked 4.5-kilometre Trollskogsstigen trail from the visitor centre, free and open at any hour.
question_context: Both sources give the same span and neither narrows it: 800 to 900 years, from the county administration of Kalmar and from the island's own visitor guide. That is the whole of what has been recorded. No girth and no height for Trolleken appears in either source, which is unusual for a tree this well known, so this page carries neither figure. If you have taped the trunk, tell us and it goes on. One story travels with the oak. A local guide records the theory that seafarers used it as a landmark, back when the ground around it was open grazing rather than the closed forest standing there now. Nobody has shown that to be true and the county's own material does not repeat it, so it stays a theory. The reserve around the tree is young by comparison: Trollskogen was established in 1998, covers 266 hectares, and has a visitor centre with parking, toilets and a cafe, plus four marked trails. There is no public transport. Route 136 runs up the island, about 65 kilometres north of Borgholm.

faq.q: What is the oldest tree in Trollskogen?
faq.a: Trolleken, the troll oak, at 800 to 900 years old. It is the oldest oak on Öland.
Nobody has published a figure. Neither the county administration nor the island's visitor guide records a girth or a height for it, so neither is given here.

faq.q: Did sailors really use the oak as a landmark?
faq.a: It is a local theory rather than a documented fact. One island guide records the idea that the tree served as a seamark when the surrounding ground was open grazing; the county administration does not repeat it.

faq.q: How do you get to Trolleken?
faq.a: By car. Route 136 runs to the top of Öland, about 65 kilometres north of Borgholm, and the marked 4.5-kilometre Trollskogsstigen starts at Naturum Trollskogen, where there is parking, toilets and a cafe. There is no public transport.

trees.story:
Öland's oldest oak is somewhere between 800 and 900 years old, and nobody has ever published how thick it is.

Trolleken stands on the Trollskogsstigen, a 4.5-kilometre marked trail through Trollskogen, the troll forest at the northeastern tip of the island. The reserve dates only from 1998 and covers 266 hectares, with a visitor centre, a cafe and four waymarked trails, and it is one of the most visited places on Öland. The tree predates all of it by eight centuries.

One story travels with the oak. A local island guide records the theory that seafarers used it as a landmark, back when the ground around it was open grazing rather than the closed forest standing there now. It is a theory and not a record: nobody has shown it to be true, and the county administration's own material does not repeat it.

What the county administration does give is the age, 800 to 900 years, and the island guide gives the same span. Neither narrows it, so neither do we. Neither gives a girth or a height either, which is unusual for a tree this well known. If you have put a tape around it, tell us and the number goes on the page.

There is no bus. Route 136 runs up the island to the naturum, about 65 kilometres north of Borgholm, with parking and a cafe at the trailhead. After that it is free, open, and on foot.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the trail: Trolleken is the veteran oak on the waymarked Trollskogsstigen, the 4.5-kilometre path from Naturum Trollskogen, and at 800 to 900 years it is the oldest oak on Öland.

best_time.label: October to November: acorns drop, and a good mast year buries the ground in them
